output.summary: KEP-6030 proposes allowing dynamic resize of memory-backed (tmpfs) emptyDir volumes via the pod /resize subresource, so the volume size can change in place alongside memory requests/limits. Its status is implementable, stage alpha, as of 2026-06-09.
output.rationale: Memory-backed emptyDir volumes are charged against container and pod memory cgroups, and users want to resize the volume together with memory limits so the volume keeps a fixed share of pod memory. The discussion settled on restricting the feature to memory-backed emptyDir (not PVCs or inline CSI ephemeral volumes) and to cgroup v2, which avoids the coordination problems of general volume expansion. Reviewers (dchen1107 approved and lgtm'd; kannon92 approved with a hold for PRR nits) accepted the design after the shrink-safety and accounting questions were answered.

alternatives.option: Generic volume expansion for all volume types (PVCs, inline CSI ephemeral volumes)
alternatives.why_not: jsafrane noted kubelet has no knowledge of CSI volume size parameters, and the KEP restricts scope to emptyDir types; msau42 said restricting to emptyDir avoids the concurrency/coordination problem.

alternatives.option: Add a top-level VolumeStatus capacity field or a generic per-volume status
alternatives.why_not: tallclair objected to EmptyDir-specific fields at the top level; natasha41575 said a generic capacity field would be confusing, so the status was placed under VolumeStatus.EmptyDir.SizeLimit.

alternatives.option: Have the kubelet create an allocatedPod object and coordinate volume and cgroup actuation through it
alternatives.why_not: natasha41575 found it more complicated while keeping strict actuation ordering between cgroups and volume mounts, and was not convinced it was better.
The discussion chose to support only cgroup v2; on cgroup v1 nodes kubelet marks the resize as Infeasible.

evidence.quote: only supporting cgroup v2 for this feature SGTM. I added to the KEP that if kubelet sees this resize request on a node with cgroup v1, it will mark the resize as `Infeasible`.
I'm not proposing that all volume resizes be done via the /resize subresource, but for specifically mem-backed volumes, the volume is considered part of the pod's memory
This kep in particular avoids the concurrency/coordination problem by restricting this to only emptyDir types.
If the volume shrink fails (usage > limit), we abort the transaction before shrinking cgroups.
I'm not sure that we want to 'generically' represent it... We could theoretically add a top-level VolumeStatus.Capacity field
